newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb explodes in India train, kills at least 12.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes in India train, kills at least 12.

text.p: A bomb blast ripped through a train in northern India on Monday, killing at least 12 passengers and injuring 37, police said.

The blast and ensuing fire destroyed two carriages just after the train pulled into Ambala cantonment near Chandigarh, capital of the northern state of Punjab, railway manager R.S. Grover told Reuters.
"It was a powerful bomb planted in one of the bogies," Ambala police chief Rajbir Deswal told Reuters in Chandigarh.
A police spokesman said 14 of the passengers were seriously injured, and several of them might not survive.
United News of India (UNI) said the train was coming from the western city of Pune and was heading towards Jammu, winter capital of the troubled northern state of Jammu and Kashmir.

Grover said the explosion occurred at 3:07 a.m. (2137 GMT Sunday), some two minutes after the train pulled into the Ambala station, an important railway junction in northern India about 40 km (25 miles) south of Chandigarh.

State government officials in Jammu and Kashmir said the bomb blast ripped through a second class sleeper carriage near the end of the train, which among its passengers was carrying some Hindu pilgrims to Jammu.
UNI said the injured had been rushed to civil, military and railway hospitals.
The Press Trust of India said the death toll was expected to rise as several passengers were believed to have been trapped in one of the compartments which caught fire.
